cases.statement: Six accession numbers in PMID 22134107 (A0041 to A0045 and A0108) in 5 families (7 alleles), citing references [50, 51]; one or more presumed homozygous (note b). By shared accession numbers, A0042 also carries c.1920delG, A0043 and A0044 c.850G>A, and A0045 c.1777C>T; A0041 and A0108 have no other listed variant.

phenotype_specificity.statement: PMID 22134107 gives no person-level clinical features or exclusion of other causes; it describes the disease only in general terms.

quotes.quote: Characteristic features are delayed separation of the umbilical cord and strong leukocytosis, especially neutrophilia, during periods of infection.
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].

de_novo.statement: Not tested in PMID 22134107. The cited source [50] has a title that mentions "recurrent and de novo mutations"; its content was not read here.

quotes.quote: Two novel frame shift, recurrent and de novo mutations in the ITGB2 (CD18) gene causing leukocyte adhesion deficiency in a highly inbred North African population

in_trans.statement: Second alleles come only from shared accession numbers in Table I (A0042: c.1920delG; A0043, A0044: c.850G>A; A0045: c.1777C>T). A0041 and A0108 are consistent with the presumed homozygous note. Phase was not shown.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Batch HGVS: single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift, p.(Asp500ThrfsTer29), agreeing with the paper's p.Asp500ThrfsX29. The paper describes the disease as caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (the β2 integrin subunit).

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.

authors_classification.statement: The variant is listed in Table I, which the authors title as mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2; no per-variant classification or ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: TABLE I: Mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2

concerns: PMID 22134107 is a mutation-update table (Table I) without case descriptions: people are identified only by database accession numbers, and sex, age and clinical features are not given per person.

In Table I the LAD-I type and the families (alleles) count belong to the table row (the variant), not to one accession number; for an accession number listed with a second variant, the expression class reflects the person's genotype, not this allele alone.

Six accession numbers in five families: at least two accession numbers are relatives. A0043 and A0044 both carry the same two listed variants (c.1498delG and c.850G>A), which suggests they are the same family (for example siblings); the table does not say.
A0042 is the same person as the c.1920delG carrier in G-lad1-006 (identity LAD1-ID0357).
A0045 is also listed under c.1777C>T (p.Arg593Cys), a row whose type is "Activated LFA-1, no CR3", while the c.1498delG row is LAD-I^o.
The cited sources [50] (title mentions recurrent and de novo mutations in a highly inbred North African population) and [51] (a Tunisian case) were not available here.
notes_for_panel: The second alleles listed for A0042 to A0045 make most of these carriers compound heterozygous per the table; only A0041 and A0108 could be the presumed homozygotes.
